sections.overview: Elops lacerta is a West African ladyfish in genus Elops and is often confused with its close relative E. senegalensis.
sections.identification: It has an elongated silvery body, 17–19 lower-arch gill rakers and 72–83 lateral-line scales.
sections.habitat: It lives in shallow West African coastal waters and enters brackish lagoons and tidal rivers.
sections.diet: It eats small fish, crustaceans and molluscs, with insects also reported for larger individuals.
sections.behavior: Juveniles occur in lagoons, while adults use estuarine, riverine and coastal waters.
sections.reproduction: Spawning is reported to take place at sea.
sections.ecology: It is a coastal predator; its close Atlantic congener E. senegalensis overlaps its range, while E. machnata lives in the Indo-West Pacific.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern.
